events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven** and troll from the shoreline out to about 50 ft, with spoons. Expected boat rating: **2 (average)**.
- **St. Joseph is a close second** (expected **2**). Fish about 20 to 40 ft of water with spoons, or small crankbaits.
- **South Haven (expected 1) and Muskegon (expected 1)** look weaker. Only go if the others are blown out.
- Run lines in the upper 50 ft of water, where the recent boat reports found fish.

## Why

- Grand Haven's most recent boat report found fish in 25 to 50 ft of water on spoons, with the Chinook catch rated below average (Grand Haven, 2024-04-24).
- St. Joseph's boat catch was rated average for coho, spread from 20 ft out past 100 ft (St. Joseph, 2024-04-17).
- Muskegon and South Haven had only below-average boat reports in the last few weeks (Muskegon, 2024-04-17; South Haven, 2024-04-17).
- I'd expect the water to keep warming a little from the 47 to 48 F buoy reading, which tends to move salmon deeper, so fish may drop below the 25 to 50 ft band over the next week.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is 6 days old, from 2024-04-24)**
- Grand Haven, 2024-04-24: boats caught "a mix of brown trout, coho salmon and the occasional Chinook salmon," with "the best water … between 25 to 50 feet deep." Chinook rated 1 (below average), coho not rated. Spoons in orange, blue and chartreuse worked (Grand Haven, 2024-04-24).
- Grand Haven, 2024-04-10: boats trolling shoreline to 50 ft caught Chinook and coho, rated 3 (good) on orange, blue and yellow spoons (Grand Haven, 2024-04-10).
- St. Joseph, 2024-04-24: boat coho not rated, and "the weather limited fishing greatly." Most boats fished 30 ft (St. Joseph, 2024-04-24).
- St. Joseph, 2024-04-17: boat coho rated 2 (average), with fish "spread out from 20 to well past 100 feet of water" (St. Joseph, 2024-04-17).
- South Haven, 2024-04-17: boat coho rated 1 in 30 ft of water (South Haven, 2024-04-17). No South Haven boat report for 2024-04-24.
- Muskegon, 2024-04-17: boat Chinook and coho rated 1, with the best action "from the shoreline out to 60 feet," on bright spoons (Muskegon, 2024-04-17).

**Past seasons (history, similar water of about 48 F; mostly May)**
- Grand Haven, 2023-05-03 (buoy 44 F): Chinook in 25 to 65 ft on glow and bright spoons, rated 3 (Grand Haven, 2023-05-03).
- St. Joseph, 2023-05-10 (buoy 49 F): Chinook in 80 ft on spoons, rated 3 (St. Joseph, 2023-05-10).
- South Haven, 2023-04-26 (buoy 45 F): boat salmon fishing rated 0 (slow) (South Haven, 2023-04-26).

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water this past week: 47 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, 48 F at St. Joseph and South Haven, each up 3 F over the week (buoys 45029 and 45168). Live data was unavailable, so this is the week before 2024-04-30 (Grand Haven, Muskegon, St. Joseph, South Haven, 2024-04-30 conditions check).
- I did not get a modeled cold-layer depth or a wind forecast, so I can't say whether a north or east wind is pushing warm water offshore.

## Caveats

- The newest report is 6 days old, and the buoy temperatures are from the week before today. Treat the ratings as expectations, not current fishing.
- Historical matches are mostly from May, so they describe what happened at similar temperatures, not what this week will bring.
- Small boat safety: the reports mention weather limiting fishing, and I have no wind forecast. Check conditions before you go.
- Ratings are my estimates from the reports, not DNR ratings.

- Grand Haven, South Haven, St. Joseph, Muskegon, 2024-04-24: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3987c22
- Grand Haven, South Haven, St. Joseph, Muskegon, 2024-04-17: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/39703c8

- South Haven, St. Joseph, 2024-04-03: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/39420c4
